compareCandidate.label: Line graph vs. bar chart
compareCandidate.description: A line graph connects ordered points to reveal a trend; a bar chart compares separate categories by height.

plainLanguageExplanation: A line graph places one dot for each data point on a grid — time usually runs left to right — then connects the dots with straight segments. The connecting line makes change visible: going up means increasing, going down means decreasing, flat means staying the same. A line graph is perfect for anything measured over time: temperature each hour, height each year, savings each month. To read it, trace the line and watch its direction — the rises and dips tell the whole story.
whyItMatters: Trends live in line graphs — the rise of temperatures, the crash of a stock, the growth of a plant. Being able to read a trend line is how you understand weather, finance, and science reporting.
didYouKnow: Line graphs for time series go back to at least the 10th century — medieval manuscripts graphed planetary movement; French astronomer Nicole Oresme drew a time graph of velocity in the 1300s.
compareReason: Students pick a chart without thinking about time — comparing the connected trend line with the category bars shows the right tool for the question.
